### What does this PR do?

Fixes #7904 for **FSDP** merged LoRA (`actor_rollout_ref.model.lora.merge=true`) with `free_cache_engine=true`. Hybrid sleep was level 2, which discards vLLM parameter storage. Wake puts the buffers back empty. The FSDP merged sync then sends a PEFT export through `load_weights`, not a full checkpoint refill, so any parameter that export does not overwrite stays uninitialized. Rollout text turns into token soup and nothing raises. `free_cache_engine=false` never discards those parameters, which is why that run stays clean.

**Megatron is unchanged:** merged LoRA still sleeps at level 2. Megatron’s merge path uses `bridge.export_hf_weights` (full HF export), so a level-2 discard is fine there. Adapter LoRA (`merge=false`) already slept at level 1 on every backend. Full-parameter training still sleeps at level 2.

This does not use `initialize_layerwise_reload` / `finalize_layerwise_reload`. That lifecycle buffers every tensor until the layer is complete and can OOM on large MoE, which #7987 already rejected in favor of in-place MoE staging.

This is not #8032 (opt-in `lora.resync_base` so adapter mode can sleep at level 2) or #7304. https://github.com/verl-project/verl/pulls?q=is%3Apr+7904

### Checklist Before Starting

- [x] Search for similar PRs. Paste at least one query link here: https://github.com/verl-project/verl/pulls?q=is%3Apr+7904
- [x] Format the PR title as `[{modules}] {type}: {description}` (This will be checked by the CI)

### Test

```
python3 -m pytest tests/utils/test_vllm_weight_name_normalization_on_cpu.py -q
```

23 passed, 4 skipped. The skips are existing `importorskip("vllm")` cases. The weight-sync path is unchanged from main.

Hybrid sleep tests (stub engine recording `sleep(level)`): 10 passed — full-param level 2; `fsdp` / `fsdp2` / `fsdp_turbo` merged level 1; `megatron` / other / unset strategy merged level 2; adapter level 1. `ruff check` and `ruff format --check` passed on the changed Python files.

No GPU rerun of the A100 case from #7904.

### API and Usage Example

No API or config change. `free_cache_engine` stays true. FSDP merged LoRA now sleeps at level 1 (CPU copy of rollout weights between steps). Megatron merged LoRA stays at level 2.

### Design & Code Changes

- `LLMServerManager` passes `actor_rollout_ref.actor.strategy` into the vLLM replica / HTTP server.
- `_resolve_sleep_level` returns 1 for merged LoRA only when that strategy is `fsdp`, `fsdp2`, or `fsdp_turbo` (shared `FSDPEngine._merged_lora_per_tensor_param` PEFT-export path). Megatron and an unset strategy stay at level 2 for merged LoRA. Adapter, MTP, and NPU stay at level 1.
- The previous layerwise reload and `mark_sleep_discarded_weights` path is removed. `update_weights_from_ipc` is back to the in-place MoE staging path from main.

### Checklist Before Submitting

- [x] Read the [Contribute Guide](https://github.com/verl-project/verl/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md).
- [ ] Full `pre-commit run --all-files` was not run. `ruff check` and `ruff format --check` passed on the changed Python files.
- [ ] Docs were not updated.
- [x] CPU coverage is the hybrid sleep tests in `.github/workflows/vllm.yml`. A GPU rerun of #7904 was not done.
- [ ] ci-request was not sent.
- [ ] Recipe submodule was not touched.

All committers have signed the CLA.
I think https://github.com/verl-project/verl/issues/7904 is a problem specific to lora instead of sleep level=2, since we didn't see any corruption in full parameter training.

Dropped the layerwise reload. Agreed this is not a general level-2 bug: full-parameter sleep stays at level 2, and weight sync is back to the in-place MoE path from #7987.

#7904 is merged LoRA (`lora.merge=true`) plus `free_cache_engine=true`. That sync is a PEFT export, not a full checkpoint refill, so a level-2 discard leaves any missed parameter uninitialized. Merged LoRA now sleeps at level 1: wake restores the parameters, then the existing merged sync overwrites them. Adapter mode is unchanged. I have not rerun the A100 repro.
Is this specific for FSDP backend? I don't reproduce the issue on Megatron backend and I think megatron backend should keep using sleep level 2 for merged lora.

Yes. Level 1 for merged LoRA is only the FSDP PEFT-export path.

#7904 used the default `ppo_trainer` (FSDP) with `lora.merge=true` and `free_cache_engine=true`. That sync goes through `FSDPEngine._merged_lora_per_tensor_param` (`normalize_peft_param_name(state_dict())`), which does not refill every parameter after sleep level 2. `fsdp`, `fsdp2`, and `fsdp_turbo` share that engine, so those still sleep at level 1 when LoRA is merged.

Megatron stays at level 2 for merged LoRA. `MegatronEngine.get_per_tensor_param` calls `bridge.export_hf_weights` on the merge path, which is a full HF export, and that matches what you see. Adapter LoRA is still level 1 on every backend. Full-parameter training is still level 2.

The HTTP server cannot tell the backend from the LoRA config, since both sides use `lora.merge`. `LLMServerManager` passes `actor_rollout_ref.actor.strategy` into the vLLM replica. An unset strategy also stays at level 2.

+        is not a full refill of a level-2 discard (#7904). ``fsdp_turbo`` uses

+        stays at level 2. An unset strategy stays at level 2 as well: only the
+        PEFT-export backends opt into level 1.
+        """
+        if not self._merged_lora():
+            return False
+        # fsdp / fsdp2 / fsdp_turbo share FSDPEngine's PEFT merge export.

         """Deepest sleep level whose discarded state a subsequent weight sync can restore.
 
-        MTP drafter-only weights are initialized by vLLM and are not guaranteed
-        to be restored by actor weight sync after level 2 sleep discards them.
-        lora only update adapter weights, so set sleep level to 1.
-        vllm_ascend not support sleep_level now. Enabling EP during training may lead to accuracy issues.
+        Level 2 discards parameter storage. A full checkpoint sync rewrites every
+        parameter, so that is the right level for full-parameter training and for
+        Megatron merged LoRA (the bridge exports a complete HF state dict).

+        Adapter sync rewrites only the adapter, so it stays at level 1. FSDP
+        merged LoRA (``model.lora.merge=true`` with ``actor.strategy`` in
+        ``fsdp`` / ``fsdp2`` / ``fsdp_turbo``) sends a PEFT export, and vLLM is
+        not started with ``enable_lora`` on that path. After a level-2 discard,
+        any parameter that export does not overwrite stays uninitialized and
+        rollout text becomes token soup (#7904). Level 1 offloads the parameters

+        MTP drafter-only weights are initialized by vLLM and are not restored by

+        EP during training may lead to accuracy issues.

+        # export, which is not a full refill of a level-2 discard (#7904).
+        if (
+            mtp_rollout_enabled
+            or self.lora_as_adapter
+            or self._fsdp_peft_merged_lora()

[![CLA assistant check](https://cla-assistant.io/pull/badge/signed)](https://cla-assistant.io/verl-project/verl?pullRequest=8046)
All committers have signed the CLA.
I think https://github.com/verl-project/verl/issues/7904 is a problem specific to lora instead of sleep level=2, since we didn't see any corruption in full parameter training.

Dropped the layerwise reload. Agreed this is not a general level-2 bug: full-parameter sleep stays at level 2, and weight sync is back to the in-place MoE path from #7987.

#7904 is merged LoRA (`lora.merge=true`) plus `free_cache_engine=true`. That sync is a PEFT export, not a full checkpoint refill, so a level-2 discard leaves any missed parameter uninitialized. Merged LoRA now sleeps at level 1: wake restores the parameters, then the existing merged sync overwrites them. Adapter mode is unchanged. I have not rerun the A100 repro.
Is this specific for FSDP backend? I don't reproduce the issue on Megatron backend and I think megatron backend should keep using sleep level 2 for merged lora.

Yes. Level 1 for merged LoRA is only the FSDP PEFT-export path.

#7904 used the default `ppo_trainer` (FSDP) with `lora.merge=true` and `free_cache_engine=true`. That sync goes through `FSDPEngine._merged_lora_per_tensor_param` (`normalize_peft_param_name(state_dict())`), which does not refill every parameter after sleep level 2. `fsdp`, `fsdp2`, and `fsdp_turbo` share that engine, so those still sleep at level 1 when LoRA is merged.

Megatron stays at level 2 for merged LoRA. `MegatronEngine.get_per_tensor_param` calls `bridge.export_hf_weights` on the merge path, which is a full HF export, and that matches what you see. Adapter LoRA is still level 1 on every backend. Full-parameter training is still level 2.

The HTTP server cannot tell the backend from the LoRA config, since both sides use `lora.merge`. `LLMServerManager` passes `actor_rollout_ref.actor.strategy` into the vLLM replica. An unset strategy also stays at level 2.
